# Introduction {#sec-intro}

This chapter introduces a synthetic problem. Imagine a family of systems that each turn a
number into another number, with some noise added on the way. The study asks how well one can
recover the input from the output.[^1] The sentences here are filler written for this example,
and they say nothing about any real field.

[^1]: A footnote with a few words, so that the footnote size and spacing can be checked.

## Motivation {#sec-motivation}

A short second section, so that the contents list has more than one level. The argument is
easy to state and easy to doubt, which is what a synthetic example needs. A reader who followed
@quill2019 would expect a plain answer, and the next chapter gives a plain answer.

> A block quote is set single spaced in the house profile and, where a guide asks for it, in
